cards.en:
Think of it like this: You buy a music CD. You own the plastic disc, but you do not own the song. The song belongs to the person who created it. That invisible ownership is called intellectual property.

The rule:

  • Intellectual Property (IP) = the creation of intellect (things made by the mind: songs, apps, inventions, logos).
  • It is a set of separate intangible asset rights. Intangible = you cannot touch it. Asset = something valuable you own.
  • The rights can be granted to a person, a party (group) or a company.
  • Four main types: copyright, patent, trademark, registered design.
  • Why protect it? So creators can earn money and keep creating.

Exam wording: IP is the creation of intellect, a set of separate intangible asset rights granted to a person, a party or a company. Protecting IP ensures a safe and fair environment for artists and inventors to continue their innovations.
cards.zh:
先这样理解：你买了一张 CD，你拥有的是那张光碟，但歌曲本身不是你的，它属于创作者。这种“看不见的拥有权”就是知识产权。

规则：

  • Intellectual Property (IP) = the creation of intellect（脑力创作：歌曲、app、发明、标志）。
  • 它是一组 separate intangible asset rights（独立的无形财产权）。intangible = 摸不到；asset = 有价值的财产。
  • 权利可以属于个人、团体（party）或公司。
  • 四大类：copyright、patent、trademark、registered design。
  • 为什么要保护？让创作者有收入，才愿意继续创作。

考试写法（Exam wording）：IP is the creation of intellect, a set of separate intangible asset rights granted to a person, a party or a company. 保护 IP 可以 ensure a safe and fair environment for artists and inventors to continue their innovations。

ex.q: A student downloads a movie for offline viewing inside a paid Netflix account. Is this legal?
ex.a:
1. The download happens inside the paid platform.
2. The platform's terms of use allow offline viewing for subscribers.
3. So it is legal: the student uses the right he paid for.
ex.az:
1. 下载是在付费平台内进行。
2. 平台条款允许订阅者离线观看。
3. 所以合法。

ex.q: Tom buys a phone game for $30. Does Tom now own the game's IP?
ex.a:
1. Tom paid for a right to use the game.
2. The game's code, art and name still belong to the developer.
3. So Tom owns a licence to play, not the IP.
ex.az:
1. Tom 付钱买的是使用权。
2. 代码、美术、名称仍属开发者。
3. Tom 不拥有 IP。

ex.q: Common mistake: "I bought the textbook, so I can photocopy the whole book and give copies to my classmates."
ex.a:
1. Owning the paper copy ≠ owning the copyright.
2. Copying a whole book and giving it out is unauthorised reproduction and distribution.
3. Right way: each classmate buys a copy, or only a small part is used for study (fair dealing).
ex.az:
1. 拥有纸本 ≠ 拥有版权。
2. 影印整本分发是未经授权的复制和分发。
3. 正确做法：各自购买，或只为学习使用小部分（fair dealing）。

cards.t: Four types of IP: overview and registration
cards.en:
Think of it like this: Think of a new phone. Its code, its clever inside technology, its brand logo and its good looks are each protected by a different kind of IP.

The rule:

TypeProtectsExampleRegister?
CopyrightAn original workSoftware, sound recording, filmNo (automatic)
PatentAn invention: product, process or substanceFacebook's dynamic mask appYes
TrademarkA unique sign that marks your goods/servicesLogo, slogan, app name, app iconYes
Registered designThe new and distinctive appearance of a productPhone shape, GUIYes

Exam wording: Except for copyright, the other types of IP all require registration. In Hong Kong, registration is done with the Intellectual Property Department.
cards.zh:
先这样理解：想象一部新手机：它的程序码、内部技术、品牌标志、外观，分别由不同的 IP 保护。

规则：

类型保护什么例子要注册？
Copyrightoriginal work 原创作品软件、录音、电影不用（自动）
Patent发明：product, process or substanceFacebook 动态面具要
Trademark区分商品/服务的独特标记标志、口号、app 名称、图标要
Registered design产品新颖独特的外观手机外形、GUI要

考试写法（Exam wording）：Except for copyright, the other types of IP all require registration.（在香港向知识产权署注册）

ex.q: A start-up invents a new battery-charging method, names it 'ZapGo', and writes control software. Match each to an IP right.
ex.a:
1. Charging method = invention (process) → patent, must register.
2. 'ZapGo' name = brand sign → trademark, must register.
3. Control software = original work → copyright, automatic.
ex.az:
1. 充电方法 → patent（要注册）。
2. 名称 → trademark（要注册）。
3. 软件 → copyright（自动）。

ex.q: A furniture company designs a chair with an unusual curved shape. Which IP protects the shape?
ex.a:
1. The shape is about how the product looks.
2. Appearance → registered design.
3. It must be registered to be protected.
ex.az:
1. 形状是外观。
2. → registered design。
3. 需注册。

ex.q: Common mistake: "I must register my school essay to get copyright."
ex.a:
1. Copyright is automatic once the work is created.
2. Only patent, trademark and registered design need registration.
3. So the essay is already protected.
ex.az:
1. 版权在作品完成时自动产生。
2. 只有另外三种要注册。
3. 文章已受保护。

demo.title: Which IP protects which part of a phone?

frames.en: The phone's operating system code is an original work → copyright (automatic).
frames.zh: 操作系统代码是原创作品 → copyright（自动）。

frames.en: A new display technology is an invention → patent (register).
frames.zh: 新屏幕技术是发明 → patent（要注册）。

frames.en: The brand logo tells buyers who made it → trademark (register).
The shape and look → registered design (register).

cards.t: Copyright symbol and patents for software
cards.en:
Think of it like this: Copyright is like a lock on the exact words you wrote. A patent is like a lock on the method: even if someone writes totally new code to do the same clever trick, the patent still stops them.

The rule:

  • Copyright = the right given to the owner of an original work. Shown with © + owner + year, e.g. © Eva Chan 2020.
  • Patent = protection of inventions: a product, process or substance.
  • Computer programs can be patented if they solve a technical problem, e.g. Facebook's dynamic mask app, Airbnb's automated booking-availability method.
  • Copyright protects the code as written; a patent protects the technical method.

Exam wording: Computer programs can be patented if they solve a technical problem. A patent protects an invention which can be a product, process or substance.
cards.zh:
先这样理解：版权像锁住你写的“那段文字”；专利像锁住“方法”：别人就算重写全新代码做同一招，专利仍然保护。

规则：

  • Copyright：原创作品拥有者的权利，用 © + 拥有者 + 年份表示，如 © Eva Chan 2020。
  • Patent：保护发明：product, process（方法）or substance（物质）。
  • Computer programs can be patented if they solve a technical problem，例如 Facebook 动态面具、Airbnb 自动判断可订房。
  • 版权保护写出来的代码；专利保护技术方法。

考试写法（Exam wording）：Computer programs can be patented if they solve a technical problem.

ex.q: Company A re-writes, with its own code, Company B's patented automatic booking-availability method. Can B act?
ex.a:
1. No code was copied → copyright does not help.
2. The method is patented.
3. Using it without a licence = patent infringement. B can act.
ex.az:
1. 没抄代码 → 版权帮不上。
2. 方法有专利。
3. 未授权使用 = 侵犯专利。

ex.q: Write a correct copyright notice for a photo by Ken Lee taken in 2024.
ex.a:
1. Symbol: ©
2. Owner: Ken Lee
3. Year: 2024
→ © Ken Lee 2024
ex.az: → © Ken Lee 2024

ex.q: Common mistake: "Software can only be protected by copyright."
ex.a:
1. This is a common misunderstanding.
2. If the program solves a technical problem, it can be patented.
3. So software may have both copyright (code) and a patent (method).
ex.az:
1. 常见误解。
2. 解决技术问题的程序可申请专利。
3. 软件可同时有版权和专利。

cards.tz: 商标（™ 与 ®）及注册外观设计
cards.en:
Think of it like this: When you see a bitten apple, you know who made the product. That sign is a trademark. How the phone looks (its curves) is a registered design.

The rule:

  • Trademark: a unique sign that distinguishes one's products or services from others'. Used for logo, slogan, app name, app icon.
  • ™ = you claim the sign as your brand (often not registered yet).
  • ® = registered trademark, only allowed after registration.
  • Registered design: protection of the new and distinctive appearance of products, e.g. phone appearance, GUI.

Exam wording: Trademark: a unique sign that distinguishes one's products or services from others'. Registered design: protection of the new and distinctive appearance of products.
cards.zh:
先这样理解：看到被咬一口的苹果，你就知道是谁的产品，这个标记就是 trademark。手机“长什么样”（曲线外形）就是 registered design。

规则：

  • Trademark：a unique sign that distinguishes one's products or services from others'，如标志、口号、app 名称、图标。
  • ™：声称是自己的品牌（多数未注册）。
  • ®：注册商标，注册后才可用。
  • Registered design：保护产品新颖独特的外观，如手机外形、GUI。

考试写法（Exam wording）：Trademark: a unique sign that distinguishes one's products or services from others'；Registered design: protection of the new and distinctive appearance of products。

ex.q: For the 'ORANGE' smartphone, match: (1) display technology (2) logo (3) appearance (4) source code.
ex.a:
(1) invention → patent
(2) brand sign → trademark
(3) look → registered design
(4) original work → copyright
ex.az: (1) patent (2) trademark (3) registered design (4) copyright

ex.q: A new bubble-tea shop prints 'SipSip™' on cups before registering. Is this allowed? When may it use ®?
ex.a:
1. ™ can be used to claim a brand without registration → allowed.
2. ® only after the trademark is registered.
ex.az:
1. 未注册可用 ™。
2. 注册后才能用 ®。

ex.q: Common mistake: "The layout and icons of an app's screen (GUI) are protected by trademark."
ex.a:
1. A GUI is about the appearance of the product.
2. The book lists GUI under registered design.
3. Only the app icon/name used as a brand sign is a trademark.
ex.az:
1. GUI 是外观。
2. 属 registered design。
3. 作为品牌标记的图标/名称才是 trademark。

cards.t: Who owns copyright? Monkey selfie and AI works
cards.tz: 谁拥有版权？猴子自拍与 AI 作品
cards.en:
Think of it like this: Copyright is a reward for human creativity. If no human created it, there may be no owner at all.

The rule:

  • 2014: a monkey took selfies with a photographer's camera.
  • The court said only works created by a human are protected under the Copyright Act.
  • So the photos are in the public domain (nobody owns copyright; anyone may use them).
  • Open question in the book: if AI writes news or music, who owns it? The AI, the programmer, owners of input material, or nobody?
  • For 'discuss' questions: state the principle → look at human contribution → check if input works were used without permission → give a reasoned conclusion.

Exam wording: Only works created by a human are protected by copyright; a work with no human author is in the public domain.
cards.zh:
先这样理解：版权是奖励“人类”的创意。没有人类创作，可能就没有拥有者。

规则：

  • 2014 年，猴子用摄影师的相机自拍。
  • 法院裁定 only works created by a human are protected。
  • 所以照片属 public domain（公有领域，任何人可用）。
  • 开放问题：AI 写的新闻/音乐，版权属于 AI、程序员、素材拥有者，还是没人？
  • 讨论题写法：讲原则 → 看人类贡献 → 看素材是否未经许可 → 给出有理由的结论。

考试写法（Exam wording）：Only works created by a human are protected by copyright；没有人类作者的作品属 public domain。

ex.q: Why can anyone use the monkey selfie on a school poster?
ex.a:
1. Copyright protects only human works.
2. The monkey is not human → no copyright owner.
3. Photo is in the public domain → no permission needed.
ex.az:
1. 只保护人类作品。
2. 猴子不是人 → 无版权人。
3. 公有领域，可自由使用。

ex.q: A user types a detailed prompt and an AI tool writes a song. Give one argument that the user may own it and one that nobody does.
ex.a:
1. For the user: the human chose and directed the content (human contribution).
2. For nobody: the actual creative work was done by a machine, and only human works are protected → public domain.
3. Conclude with your reasoned view; the book has no single fixed answer.
ex.az:
1. 用户有人类贡献。
2. 实际创作由机器完成 → 可能属公有领域。
3. 给出有理由的结论。

ex.q: Common mistake: "The photographer owns the monkey selfie because it is his camera."
ex.a:
1. Owning the tool does not make you the author.
2. The court held only human-created works are protected, and the monkey pressed the button.
3. So the photo is public domain, not the photographer's.
ex.az:
1. 拥有工具 ≠ 作者。
2. 按下快门的是猴子。
3. 照片属公有领域。

cards.en:
Think of it like this: The moment you finish drawing a picture, it is already yours by law, like a name tag that appears by itself. No form to fill in.

The rule:

  • Copyright is automatically given to the author or creator after the work is completed.
  • In Hong Kong, there is no need to register for copyright.
  • Copyright lasts until 50 years after the death of the creator (in general).
  • After that, the work enters the public domain.
  • A © notice is good practice, not legally required.

Exam wording: The copyright of a work is automatically given to the creator after the work is completed; there is no need to register. It generally lasts until 50 years after the death of the creator.
cards.zh:
先这样理解：你画完一幅画的那一刻，法律上它已经是你的，像名牌自动出现，不用填表。

规则：

  • 作品完成后，版权自动属于作者。
  • 香港 no need to register for copyright。
  • Copyright lasts until 50 years after the death of the creator（一般情况）。
  • 之后进入 public domain。
  • © 声明是好习惯，但 not legally required。

考试写法（Exam wording）：Copyright is automatically given to the creator after the work is completed; no registration is needed; it generally lasts until 50 years after the death of the creator.

ex.q: A composer died in 1990. Until about when is his music protected?
ex.a:
1. Rule: 50 years after death.
2. 1990 + 50 = 2040.
3. After that → public domain.

ex.q: Cindy uploads photos to social media without '© All rights reserved'. Who owns the copyright?
ex.a:
1. Copyright is automatic.
2. No declaration is needed.
3. Cindy owns it; the social media company does not become the owner.
ex.az:
1. 自动产生。
2. 无需声明。
3. Cindy 拥有。

ex.q: Common mistake: "Copyright lasts 50 years from when the work was made."
ex.a:
1. Wrong starting point.
2. It counts from the death of the creator.
3. E.g. a song written in 1980 by a singer who dies in 2030 is protected until about 2080.
ex.az:
1. 起点错了。
2. 从作者去世起计 50 年。
3. 例：2030 年去世 → 约 2080 年。

cards.t: Works protected by the Copyright Ordinance
cards.en:
Think of it like this: The law sorts protected works into three boxes: things you write/draw/compose, things you record or broadcast, and the layout of a published page.

The rule:

GroupExamples
Original literary, dramatic, musical or artistic worksComputer programs, databases, photographs, essays, lyrics
Sound recordings, broadcasts, films, cable programmesSongs, vlogs, movies, TV shows
Typographical arrangement of published editionsInterface layout of a published website, layout of a novel
  • Computer programs and databases count as literary works.
  • Not protected: ideas themselves; works not made by humans.

Exam wording: The Copyright Ordinance protects original literary, dramatic, musical or artistic works; sound recordings, broadcasts, films or cable programmes; and the typographical arrangement of published editions.
cards.zh:
先这样理解：法律把受保护作品分成三个盒子：写/画/作曲的、录制或广播的、出版物的排版。

规则：

类别例子
Original literary, dramatic, musical or artistic works程序、数据库、照片、文章、歌词
Sound recordings, broadcasts, films, cable programmes歌曲、vlog、电影、电视节目
Typographical arrangement（排印编排）of published editions已发布网站的界面布局、小说排版
  • 程序和数据库属 literary works。
  • 不保护：意念本身、非人类作品。

考试写法（Exam wording）：三类：literary, dramatic, musical or artistic works；sound recordings, broadcasts, films or cable programmes；typographical arrangement of published editions。

ex.q: Classify: (a) a mobile game's source code (b) a YouTube vlog (c) the page layout of a published e-book.
ex.a:
(a) computer program → literary work
(b) → film / sound recording
(c) → typographical arrangement
ex.az: (a) literary work (b) film (c) typographical arrangement

ex.q: A school's student database (names, classes, marks) is built by staff. Is it protected?
ex.a:
1. Databases are listed as literary works.
2. Built by humans → original work.
3. Yes, it is protected by copyright.
ex.az: 数据库属 literary work，受保护。

ex.q: Common mistake: "Only the words of a novel are protected, so I can copy its page layout freely."
ex.a:
1. The typographical arrangement of a published edition is protected separately.
2. Copying the exact layout (e.g. scanning pages) can infringe even if the text is old.
3. Right idea: both text and published layout can be protected.
ex.az:
1. 排版另受保护。
2. 扫描复制排版可能侵权。

cards.tz: 误解：意念 vs 表达
cards.en:
Think of it like this: Lots of people have the idea "take sunset photos". Nobody can own that idea. But your sunset photo, the real thing you made, is yours.

The rule:

  • Copyright does not protect ideas.
  • It protects the expression of ideas when presented in a tangible form (written, recorded, drawn, coded).
  • The idea of a to-do-list app is free; copying another app's code or icons is infringement.
  • A clever technical method may still be protected by a patent if registered.

Exam wording: Copyright does not protect ideas. It protects the expression of ideas when it is presented in a tangible form.
cards.zh:
先这样理解：很多人都有“拍日落”这个意念，没人能拥有它。但你拍出来的那张照片是你的。

规则：

  • Copyright does not protect ideas.
  • It protects the expression of ideas in a tangible form（写下、录下、画出、编成代码）。
  • “待办事项 app”这个点子人人可做；抄别人代码或图标就侵权。
  • 技术方法可另申请 patent。

考试写法（Exam wording）：Copyright does not protect ideas. It protects the expression of ideas when it is presented in a tangible form.

ex.q: Tom writes his own note app from scratch with similar features, but his own code and icons. Infringement?
ex.a:
1. Features/idea are not protected.
2. Tom copied no code, text or graphics.
3. Not copyright infringement (unless a patent/design is involved).
ex.az:
1. 意念不受保护。
2. 没抄任何表达。
3. 不侵权。

ex.q: Amy copies 200 lines of another game's code, then changes the variable names. Infringement?
ex.a:
1. The expression (code structure and logic as written) is copied.
2. Renaming variables does not make it her own expression.
3. Yes, likely infringement.
ex.az: 改变量名仍是抄袭表达，侵权。

ex.q: Common mistake: "I had the idea for this story first, so the film that used a similar plot broke my copyright."
ex.a:
1. An idea or general plot is not protected.
2. Only copying the actual expression (your text, scenes, dialogue) is infringement.
3. Without copied expression, no copyright claim.
ex.az: 意念/大纲不受保护，要抄了实际表达才侵权。

cards.en:
Think of it like this: Owning copyright is like owning a house: you decide who may enter (use it), you can rent it out (licence for royalties), sell it, or leave it to your children.

The rule:

  • Copy, publish, broadcast, adapt and translate the work.
  • Grant the right to use the work in return for royalties (版税) or other payments.
  • Sell the copyright.
  • Pass the copyright to others in a will.
  • Take legal action against infringement and obtain monetary compensation.

Exam wording: The copyright owner has exclusive rights to copy, publish, broadcast, adapt and translate the work, grant the right to use it in return for royalties, sell it and pass it to others in a will.
cards.zh:
先这样理解：拥有版权像拥有房子：你决定谁能用、可以出租（授权收版税）、可以卖、可以留给子女。

规则：

  • Copy, publish, broadcast, adapt and translate。
  • Grant the right to use … in return for royalties（收版税授权）。
  • Sell 版权。
  • Pass … in a will（遗嘱传承）。
  • 可采取法律行动并获得金钱赔偿。

考试写法（Exam wording）：exclusive rights：copy, publish, broadcast, adapt and translate; grant the right to use for royalties; sell; pass in a will。

ex.q: Peter writes a program himself. Which can he do? (1) translate and publish it (2) charge a licence fee (3) sell the copyright (4) transfer it to others.
ex.a:
1. (1) adapt/translate/publish ✔
2. (2) grant use for payment ✔
3. (3) sell ✔
4. (4) transfer, e.g. in a will ✔
→ All four.
ex.az: 四项皆可。

ex.q: A shop plays a singer's song in a TV ad without asking. What can the singer's label do?
ex.a:
1. Broadcasting is an exclusive right.
2. No permission was given → infringement.
3. Label can take legal action and claim monetary compensation.
ex.az: 可采取法律行动并索偿。

ex.q: Common mistake: "Copyright owners cannot transfer their copyrights."
ex.a:
1. False.
2. Copyright can be sold or passed in a will.
3. It is a transferable asset.
ex.az: 错。可出售或遗赠。

cards.en:
Think of it like this: Asking every creator for permission is slow. CC is like a sticker on the work saying "you may use this, as long as you follow these rules".

The rule:

  • CC licences protect both creators and users.
  • BY (Attribution): give credit to the creator.
  • SA (Share-alike): if you adapt it, share your new work under the same licence.
  • NC (Non-commercial): no commercial use.
  • ND (No Derivative Works): no changes; share only the original.
  • Combined like CC BY-SA, CC BY-NC, CC BY-ND. The creator still owns copyright ('Some rights reserved').

Exam wording: Creative Commons licences are established to protect both creators and users. Elements: Attribution, Share-alike, Non-commercial, No Derivative Works.
cards.zh:
先这样理解：每次都问作者太慢。CC 就像贴在作品上的贴纸：“你可以用，只要遵守这些规则”。

规则：

  • CC licences protect both creators and users.
  • BY：要注明作者。
  • SA：改编后要用相同授权分享。
  • NC：不可商业用途。
  • ND：不可修改，只能原样分享。
  • 组合：CC BY-SA、CC BY-NC、CC BY-ND。作者仍拥有版权。

考试写法（Exam wording）：CC licences protect both creators and users；四元素：Attribution, Share-alike, Non-commercial, No Derivative Works。

ex.q: Janice wants a CC BY-ND picture for a friend's photo book. What must she do and not do?
ex.a:
1. BY → give credit (title, creator, licence).
2. ND → do not crop, edit or modify it.
3. No NC → commercial use is allowed.
ex.az:
1. 注明出处。
2. 不可修改。
3. 可商用。

ex.q: Ken remixes a CC BY-SA song. Under what licence must he share his remix?
ex.a:
1. SA = share-alike.
2. The remix must use the same licence: CC BY-SA.
3. He must also credit the original creator.
ex.az: 须用 CC BY-SA 并注明作者。

ex.q: Common mistake: "It's CC licensed, so it has no copyright and I can do anything."
ex.a:
1. CC does not remove copyright.
2. The creator grants only some rights.
3. E.g. using a CC BY-NC image in a paid advert breaks NC → infringement.
ex.az: CC 不等于无版权；违反 NC 等条件即侵权。

frames.en: You must credit the creator: title, creator, licence.
You may not use it to make money (e.g. paid adverts).
If you change it, your new version must also be CC BY-NC-SA.
Allowed: a credited, non-profit remix shared under the same licence.
frames.zh: 允许：注明出处、非牟利、同授权的改编。

cards.en:
Think of it like this: Piracy used to mean fake DVDs at a street stall. Today the same stealing happens with one click: a free 'cracked' app, an illegal stream, a shared download link.

The rule:

  • Piracy is the unauthorised use and reproduction of copyrighted works, e.g. photocopying, counterfeit goods (冒牌商品).
  • Unauthorised use and redistribution in digital form are also considered Internet piracy.
  • Examples: watching pirated videos on streaming sites; downloading pirated games from social media, file-sharing sites, cloud or P2P sharing software; buying a cracked version or membership on online shopping sites.
  • Cases: fansub group arrested (nearly 16 million yuan illegal income, 2021); game company sued console hackers.

Exam wording: Unauthorised use and redistribution of copyrighted works in digital form are considered Internet piracy.
cards.zh:
先这样理解：以前盗版是街边的翻版碟，现在一按就有：破解 app、非法串流、分享下载链接。

规则：

  • Piracy：未经授权使用和复制版权作品，如影印、counterfeit goods（冒牌商品）。
  • Unauthorised use and redistribution in digital form are also considered Internet piracy.
  • 例子：在串流网站看盗版影片；从社交媒体、分享网站、云端、P2P 下载盗版游戏；在网购平台买破解版或会员。
  • 个案：字幕组被捕（非法收入近 1600 万元）。

考试写法（Exam wording）：Unauthorised use and redistribution in digital form are considered Internet piracy.

ex.q: A 'lifetime premium membership' of a paid app costs $20 on a shopping site, but the official price is $300/year. Piracy?
ex.a:
1. The seller is not the copyright owner.
2. It is a cracked membership sold illegally online.
3. Buying it = Internet piracy.
ex.az: 非官方破解会员 → 盗版。

ex.q: Ben uses BitTorrent (P2P) to download a new film. While downloading, his PC also uploads parts to others. Which piracy acts?
ex.a:
1. Downloading a pirated copy = unauthorised use/reproduction.
2. P2P also uploads pieces = unauthorised redistribution.
3. Both are Internet piracy.
ex.az: 下载 + P2P 同时上传 = 使用及分发，皆属盗版。

ex.q: Common mistake: "I only streamed it, I didn't download it, so it's not piracy."
ex.a:
1. The book lists watching or listening to pirated music or videos on streaming websites as piracy.
2. Streaming from an unauthorised source is still unauthorised use.
3. Right way: use licensed platforms.
ex.az: 在盗版串流网站观看也属盗版。

cards.en:
Think of it like this: A 'free' cracked app is like a free meal from a stranger: you don't know what was put in it, and nobody will help if you get sick.

The rule:

  • Security risks: malware infection and data breach (cracked files may hide viruses, trojans, spyware).
  • No technical support from the copyright owner.
  • Cannot install official updates / bug fixes → attacked through unpatched holes.
  • Legal risk: civil lawsuit or criminal prosecution.

Exam wording: Pirated software may contain malware, cannot receive security updates or technical support, and using it is copyright infringement.
cards.zh:
先这样理解：“免费”破解软件像陌生人送的饭：不知道加了什么，出事也没人帮你。

规则：

  • 安全风险：malware infection、data breach。
  • 没有技术支持。
  • 无法安装官方更新/修补，漏洞易被攻击。
  • 法律风险：民事诉讼或刑事检控。

考试写法（Exam wording）：Pirated software may contain malware, cannot receive security updates or technical support, and using it is copyright infringement.

ex.q: Janice's sister tells her not to install a 'trial version' uploaded by a blogger to cloud storage. Give TWO reasons.
ex.a:
1. Not from the official source → may be modified and contain malware → data breach.
2. Using an unauthorised copy may infringe copyright; no updates or support.
ex.az:
1. 可能含恶意程序。
2. 可能侵权，无更新支持。

ex.q: Patrick buys cracked software at half price. List possible consequences.
ex.a:
1. Computer may be attacked because bug-fix updates cannot be installed.
2. He violates IP rights.
3. Software may contain viruses.
ex.az: 无法更新被攻击；侵权；可能含病毒。

ex.q: Common mistake: "A consequence is that the copyright owner offers Patrick a customised free trial."
ex.a:
1. This is not a consequence of piracy (Checkpoint 3.2).
2. The owner gives pirates no support or offers.
3. Real consequences: malware, no updates, legal risk.
ex.az: 这不是后果。真正后果：恶意程序、无更新、法律风险。

cards.en:
Think of it like this: If everyone copies a singer's album for free, the singer earns nothing and stops making music. The copier gets caught and shamed. The whole city gets a bad name.

The rule:

GroupImpact
CreatorsNo income or motivation to continue creating new, high-quality designs
PiratesPunished, even expelled from school/company; reputation damaged
CountryDeclining reputation; difficulties in the global market

Exam wording: Name the stakeholder + the effect: "Creators lose income, so they lose motivation to create new high-quality works."
cards.zh:
先这样理解：如果大家都免费复制歌手的专辑，歌手没收入就不再创作；抄的人被抓、名誉受损；整个地方名声变差。

规则：

对象影响
Creatorsno income or motivation to continue creating
Pirates受罚、甚至被开除；reputation damaged
Countrydeclining reputation；difficulties in the global market

考试写法（Exam wording）：写法：对象 + 影响，如 "Creators lose income, so they lose motivation to create new high-quality works."

ex.q: A student shares pirated design software in the student union. One impact on the student, one on creators.
ex.a:
1. Student: may be punished or expelled; reputation damaged.
2. Creators: lose income → less motivation to develop software.
ex.az: 学生：受罚/开除；创作者：失收入、失动力。

ex.q: A city is known for selling fake branded goods. Social impact on the city?
ex.a:
1. Stakeholder = country/city.
2. Declining reputation.
3. Difficulties in the global market (partners distrust it).
ex.az: 名声下降，难打入国际市场。

ex.q: Common mistake: answering "social impact" with just "it is bad for society".
ex.a:
1. Too vague, no marks.
2. Name a stakeholder (creators/pirates/country) and a specific effect.
3. E.g. "Pirates may be expelled and their reputation damaged."
ex.az: 太空泛。要写对象 + 具体影响。

cards.en:
Think of it like this: Like dominoes: one falls, then the next. Piracy knocks down sales, then investment, then jobs, then tax.

The rule:

  1. Decrease in sales of copyrighted goods.
  2. No more investors and sponsors.
  3. Business closure leads to higher unemployment rate.
  4. The country's tax revenue falls.

Exam wording: Write it as a chain with 'so': "Piracy reduces sales, so companies earn less and investors withdraw; companies close, raising unemployment, and tax revenue falls."
cards.zh:
先这样理解：像骨牌：盗版推倒销量 → 投资 → 就业 → 税收。

规则：

  1. Decrease in sales（销量下降）。
  2. No more investors and sponsors。
  3. Business closure leads to higher unemployment rate。
  4. Tax revenue falls。

考试写法（Exam wording）：写成因果链："Piracy reduces sales, so … investors withdraw; companies close, raising unemployment, and tax revenue falls."

ex.q: Explain how widespread game piracy could affect a city's economy (3 marks).
ex.a:
1. Sales of legal games fall.
2. Studios earn less → investors/sponsors leave.
3. Studios close → unemployment rises; tax revenue falls.
ex.az: 销量跌 → 投资者撤 → 倒闭失业 → 税收减。

ex.q: A film studio's DVD sales drop 60% due to piracy. What happens next in the chain?
ex.a:
1. Studio becomes unprofitable.
2. No new investors for the next film.
3. Staff laid off; government gets less tax.
ex.az: 无利润 → 无投资 → 裁员、税收减。

ex.q: Common mistake: listing "sales, investors, unemployment, tax" as four separate words.
ex.a:
1. Lists without links get few marks.
2. Show cause → effect with 'so' / 'leads to'.
3. Each step must explain why the next happens.
ex.az: 要写因果关系，不只列词。

frames.en: People use pirated copies instead of buying.
The business is not profitable, so no more investors and sponsors.
frames.zh: 无利润 → 投资者撤走。

frames.en: Business closure leads to a higher unemployment rate.
Fewer businesses and workers → the country's tax revenue falls.

cards.en:
Think of it like this: Selling pirated copies is not just 'naughty'. In Hong Kong it is a crime, like theft, and you can go to jail.

The rule:

  • Goal: maintain a balance between the interests of copyright holders and society.
  • Under the Copyright Ordinance, distributing and using pirated media and software for commercial purposes are criminal offences.
  • Maximum penalty for selling pirated copies: a fine of $50,000 per copy and imprisonment for 4 years.
  • Examples: selling infringing films online; importing/exporting pirated software; live streaming songs without permission; designing graphics for work with pirated software.
  • Non-commercial distribution is also a crime if it harms the copyright owner's interest.

Exam wording: Distributing and using pirated media and software for commercial purposes are criminal offences; maximum penalty: $50,000 per pirated copy and 4 years' imprisonment.
cards.zh:
先这样理解：卖盗版不只是“顽皮”，在香港是刑事罪，可以坐牢。

规则：

  • 目的：balance between the interests of copyright holders and society。
  • 《版权条例》：distributing and using pirated media and software for commercial purposes are criminal offences。
  • 最高罚则：每份盗版罚款 $50,000 及监禁 4 年。
  • 例：网上卖盗版电影、进出口盗版软件、未经许可直播歌曲、工作中用盗版软件设计图像。
  • 非商业分发如损害版权人利益也属刑事罪。

考试写法（Exam wording）：… for commercial purposes are criminal offences; max $50,000 per copy + 4 years' imprisonment.

ex.q: A shop owner sells 3 pirated game discs. Maximum penalty?
ex.a:
1. $50,000 per copy.
2. 3 × $50,000 = $150,000.
3. Plus up to 4 years in prison.

ex.q: A designer uses pirated Photoshop to make paid posters for clients. Criminal?
ex.a:
1. Using pirated software for commercial purposes (paid work).
2. The book lists 'designing graphics for work with pirated software'.
3. Yes, a criminal offence.
ex.az: 商业用途用盗版 → 刑事罪。

ex.q: Common mistake: "It's only a crime if you sell it. Sharing for free is always fine."
ex.a:
1. Non-commercial distribution is also a crime if it harms the copyright owner's interest.
2. E.g. the BT case: sharing films for free led to 3 months' jail.
3. Free sharing can still be criminal.
ex.az: 免费分享若损害版权人利益也属刑事罪（如 BT 案）。

cards.t: Civil lawsuit and the BT case
cards.tz: 民事诉讼与 BT 案
cards.en:
Think of it like this: Two different doors to court. The government can punish you (criminal). The owner can also sue you for money (civil).

The rule:

Criminal offenceCivil lawsuit
Who starts itGovernment (Customs)Copyright owner
OutcomeFine (up to $50,000/copy) + jail (4 yrs)Monetary compensation
  • Copyright owners have the right to ask the buyers or users for monetary compensation through a civil lawsuit.
  • Hong Kong BT case (Big Crook / 古惑天皇案): a user was sentenced to 3 months in prison for distributing copyrighted films using BT.

Exam wording: Copyright owners have the right to ask buyers or users for monetary compensation through a civil lawsuit.
cards.zh:
先这样理解：上法庭有两扇门：政府检控你（刑事），版权人告你要钱（民事）。

规则：

刑事民事
谁提出政府（海关）版权拥有者
结果罚款 + 监禁金钱赔偿
  • Copyright owners … ask the buyers or users for monetary compensation through a civil lawsuit.
  • BT 案（古惑天皇案）：用 BT 分发电影，判监禁 3 个月。

考试写法（Exam wording）：monetary compensation through a civil lawsuit

ex.q: Criminal case vs civil lawsuit: who starts it and what outcome?
ex.a:
1. Criminal: government (C&ED) prosecutes → fine/jail.
2. Civil: copyright owner sues → monetary compensation.
ex.az: 刑事：政府检控 → 罚/监；民事：版权人起诉 → 赔偿。

ex.q: You share a commercial Chinese input software with friends through a cloud drive. What may happen?
ex.a:
1. Unauthorised distribution.
2. The owner may sue you for copyright infringement through a civil lawsuit.
ex.az: 可能被民事起诉。

ex.q: Common mistake: "The BT user was only distributing, not selling, so he could only be sued for money."
ex.a:
1. He was sentenced to 3 months in prison (criminal).
2. P2P sharing that harms owners can be a crime even without selling.
3. Both criminal and civil routes are possible.
ex.az: BT 案判监，证明不卖也可犯刑事罪。

frames.en: Someone distributes pirated films.
Customs investigates and prosecutes → fine/jail.
frames.zh: 海关调查检控 → 罚款/监禁。

frames.en: The copyright owner sues → monetary compensation.
frames.zh: 版权人起诉 → 金钱赔偿。

cards.t: IP authorities: IPD vs Customs and Excise
cards.tz: 知识产权署 vs 香港海关
cards.en:
Think of it like this: IPD is like the teacher and the registry office: it writes rules, keeps records, and teaches. Customs is like the police: it catches and punishes.

The rule:

AuthorityRole
Intellectual Property Department (IPD)Advising on policies and legislation; registration of trademarks, patents, designs and copyright licensing bodies; promotion and education
Customs and Excise Department (C&ED)Taking criminal sanctions against copyright and trademark infringements
  • Selling cracked apps online may be a criminal offence; C&ED can act even if the owner does not complain.
  • 2018: Customs acted against consoles preloaded with 5,000+ pirated games.

Exam wording: Only the Customs and Excise Department takes criminal sanctions against copyright and trademark infringements.
cards.zh:
先这样理解：知识产权署像老师兼登记处：订政策、管注册、做教育。海关像警察：执法惩罚。

规则：

部门职能
IPD政策及立法建议；注册商标、专利、设计及版权授权团体；推广教育
C&EDtaking criminal sanctions（刑事制裁）
  • 网上卖破解 app 可能是刑事罪；版权人没投诉，海关也可执法。

考试写法（Exam wording）：Only the Customs and Excise Department takes criminal sanctions.

ex.q: A tutor photocopies a whole book for students. To whom can the copyright holder complain?
ex.a:
1. This is a criminal-type infringement.
2. Criminal sanctions → Customs and Excise Department.
ex.az: 向香港海关投诉。

ex.q: A company wants to register its new logo. Which authority?
ex.a:
1. Registration of trademarks.
2. → IPD.
ex.az: IPD 负责注册。

ex.q: Common mistake: "The IPD arrests people who sell pirated software."
ex.a:
1. IPD does policy, registration and education only.
2. Only C&ED takes criminal sanctions (not IPD, not OGCIO).
ex.az: 执法的是海关，不是 IPD。

cards.en:
Think of it like this: A teacher shows one short clip in class to explain a point. Asking the film company first every time would be silly, so the law allows small, fair uses.

The rule:

  • The Copyright Ordinance protects not only copyright owners but also users.
  • Exceptions allow limited use of a copyrighted work without the owner's permission.
  • Fair dealing purposes: education; non-commercial research and private study; criticism, review and news reporting.
  • Key: limited use, permitted purpose, normally non-profit, does not replace the original.

Exam wording: Fair dealing allows limited use of a copyrighted work without the permission of the copyright owner for purposes such as education, research and private study, criticism, review and news reporting.
cards.zh:
先这样理解：老师在课上播一小段片段讲解，每次都先问电影公司很不合理，所以法律容许小量、公平的使用。

规则：

  • 条例保护的不只是版权人，也保护用户。
  • Exceptions allow limited use … without permission.
  • Fair dealing 用途：education；non-commercial research and private study；criticism, review and news reporting。
  • 关键：小量、合资格用途、非牟利、不取代原作。

考试写法（Exam wording）：Fair dealing allows limited use without permission for education, research and private study, criticism, review and news reporting.

ex.q: A YouTuber shows a 10-second phone advert clip while reviewing the camera quality. Which purpose?
ex.a:
1. Limited clip.
2. Used to evaluate a product.
3. → Criticism, review.
ex.az: 评论用途。

ex.q: A student copies one chart from a journal into private study notes. Fair dealing?
ex.a:
1. Small part.
2. Purpose: private study, non-commercial.
3. Likely fair dealing.
ex.az: 小部分、私人研习 → 公平处理。

ex.q: Common mistake: "Anything for education is fair dealing."
ex.a:
1. Not all educational acts are exempt.
2. E.g. distributing a whole e-textbook to students is infringement.
3. Must be limited and not replace buying the original.
ex.az: 教育用途也要有限度，整本分发即侵权。

cards.t: Fair dealing or infringement? School cases
cards.tz: 公平处理还是侵权？学校个案
cards.en:
Think of it like this: Ask four quick questions, like a checklist at the door: How much? For money? Does it replace buying? Is it relevant to learning?

The rule:

Not fair dealingFair dealing
Distributing the whole e-textbookShowing parts of movies for instruction
Using software for assignment without a proper licenceAttaching copyrighted images to an assignment
Copying code and claiming it as your ownPrinting a piece of a journal article for personal study
  • Tests: amount (part vs whole), commercial?, replaces buying?, relevant to the course?

Exam wording: Not all acts for educational purposes can be exempted; only limited, non-profit use relevant to teaching is fair dealing.
cards.zh:
先这样理解：用四个问题检查：用了多少？赚钱吗？会取代购买吗？与学习相关吗？

规则：

不是公平处理公平处理
分发整本电子书播放电影部分片段教学
无合法授权用软件做功课功课中附上版权图片
抄代码当自己作品打印期刊一部分自修

考试写法（Exam wording）：Not all acts for educational purposes can be exempted.

ex.q: Which is fair dealing? A. Copy an entire web article into an assignment B. Show an entire film in class C. Play a few minutes of a documentary to illustrate history D. Distribute HKDSE past papers free
ex.a:
1. A, B, D use whole works → replace the original.
2. C uses a small part for instruction.
3. Answer: C.
ex.az: 答案 C。

ex.q: A teacher shows a 3-minute TV clip on air pollution in a Geography lesson. Fair?
ex.a: 1. Part only. 2. For instruction. 3. Non-commercial, relevant → fair dealing.
ex.az: 公平处理。

ex.q: Common mistake: "I used a cracked copy of video software only for a school assignment, so it's fair dealing."
ex.a:
1. Fair dealing covers using parts of works, not using unlicensed software.
2. Using software without a proper licence is not fair dealing.
3. Use a free/education licence instead.
ex.az: 无授权软件做功课不是公平处理。

cards.t: When the dealing is unfair: news cases
cards.tz: 不公平处理的新闻个案
cards.en:
Think of it like this: Using a topic like 'education' or 'review' as a label does not make copying fair. If you make money and copy the whole thing, it's unfair.

The rule:

  • Selling pirated HKDSE teaching notes (2020): Customs acted. Commercial + whole work → not fair dealing.
  • 'Fast movies' in Japan (2021): edited short versions revealing the whole plot, earning ad revenue. Substitutes the film + profit → not fair.
  • Peter's photos: publisher in textbook (commercial) and friend reposting without permission → illegal; teacher using one photo in a lesson, friend printing with permission → legal.

Exam wording: It is not fair dealing because it is for commercial purposes and reproduces the whole work, so it replaces the market for the original.
cards.zh:
先这样理解：贴上“教育”或“评论”标签不等于公平。赚钱又整份复制就不公平。

规则：

  • 卖盗版 DSE 笔记（2020）：商业 + 整份 → 不公平。
  • 日本“快速电影”（2021）：剪辑透露全部剧情，赚广告费 → 不公平。
  • Peter 的照片：出版社放入课本、朋友未经许可转发 → 违法；老师课上用一张、朋友获许可打印 → 合法。

考试写法（Exam wording）：for commercial purposes、reproduces the whole work、replaces the market for the original。

ex.q: A student uploads a 10-minute video summarising a new movie scene by scene and earns ad revenue. Fair dealing?
ex.a:
1. Reveals essentially the whole work.
2. Earns profit.
3. Viewers may skip the film → not fair dealing.
ex.az: 整部内容 + 牟利 → 不是。

ex.q: A publisher puts Peter's photo in a textbook without asking. Legal?
ex.a:
1. Commercial use (textbook is sold).
2. No permission.
3. Illegal.
ex.az: 商业使用未获许可 → 违法。

ex.q: Common mistake: "The notes are for DSE study, so selling copies is educational fair dealing."
ex.a:
1. The subject being educational does not matter.
2. Selling = commercial; copying whole notes replaces the original.
3. Not fair dealing; Customs took action.
ex.az: 科目是教育不代表是公平处理；售卖即商业。

cards.en:
Think of it like this: Borrowing a friend's bike: find out whose it is, ask, ride it the way they allow, and say thanks. Using someone's work is the same.

The rule:

  1. Identify the copyright owners.
  2. Obtain permissions or licences.
  3. Use the work according to the terms of use.
  4. Acknowledge the source properly.
  • Read the terms and conditions before using the copyrighted material.
  • Both users and holders share responsibility; IPD promotes IP awareness.

Exam wording: Users should obtain permission from the copyright holders and read the terms and conditions before using the copyrighted material: identify, obtain, use according to terms, acknowledge.
cards.zh:
先这样理解：借朋友的单车：先知道是谁的、问一声、照他说的方式骑、再说谢谢。用别人的作品也一样。

规则：

  1. Identify 版权拥有者。
  2. Obtain 许可或授权。
  3. Use 按使用条款使用。
  4. Acknowledge 注明出处。
  • 使用前阅读条款。

考试写法（Exam wording）：Identify the owner, obtain permission/licence, use according to the terms, acknowledge the source.

ex.q: A school club wants to play a pop song in its promo video. Apply the four steps.
ex.a:
1. Identify: record company/composer.
2. Obtain permission or buy a licence.
3. Use within the licence (length, platform).
4. Credit title, artist, licence.
ex.az: 识别 → 取得授权 → 按条款 → 注明。

ex.q: John wants a song for his vlog but cannot afford a licence. Alternative?
ex.a:
1. Choose royalty-free or CC-licensed music.
2. Follow its licence terms (e.g. BY → credit).
3. Credit the song.
ex.az: 选用免版税或 CC 音乐，并遵守条款。

ex.q: Common mistake: "I gave credit to the artist in my video, so I don't need permission."
ex.a:
1. Crediting is only step 4.
2. Without permission/licence (step 2), it is still infringement.
3. Credit ≠ permission.
ex.az: 注明出处不等于获得许可。

frames.en: Who owns this work? (artist, label, photographer)
Ask for permission or buy a licence (or pick a CC work).
Use only as the terms allow (e.g. non-commercial, no edits).
Credit title, creator and licence.

cards.tz: 注明出处与 CC 署名
cards.en:
Think of it like this: Saying "photo by Mary" is like saying thank you in public. For CC works, it is not just polite, it's required.

The rule:

  • Giving credit acknowledges the copyright owners' effort and helps avoid copyright infringement and plagiarism.
  • Attribution is required under CC licences.
  • Order: Title – Creator – Licence (TCL): "Cat" by Y.Hino is licensed under CC BY 2.0.
  • Add links to the original and the licence where possible.

Exam wording: "[Title]" by [Creator] is licensed under [Licence].
cards.zh:
先这样理解：写“相片：Mary”就像公开说谢谢。对 CC 作品来说，这不只是礼貌，而是必须的。

规则：

  • 注明出处可肯定版权人的努力，并避免侵权和抄袭。
  • CC 授权规定要署名。
  • 顺序：Title – Creator – Licence："Cat" by Y.Hino is licensed under CC BY 2.0.
  • 尽量附上原作及授权链接。

考试写法（Exam wording）："[Title]" by [Creator] is licensed under [Licence].

ex.q: Write an attribution: photo 'Victoria Harbour Night' by Chan Siu Ming, CC BY-NC 4.0.
ex.a:
1. Title in quotes.
2. 'by' + creator.
3. 'is licensed under' + licence.
→ "Victoria Harbour Night" by Chan Siu Ming is licensed under CC BY-NC 4.0.
ex.az: 按 TCL 顺序写。

ex.q: Attribution for image '20160314-ZD4_6150' by zhao hui, CC BY-SA 2.0.
ex.a:
→ "20160314-ZD4_6150" by zhao hui is licensed under CC BY-SA 2.0.
If adapted, share under CC BY-SA too.
ex.az: 如改编，亦须以 CC BY-SA 分享。

ex.q: Common mistake: writing only "Image from Google".
ex.a:
1. Google is a search engine, not the creator.
2. Missing title, creator and licence.
3. Find the real source and write TCL.
ex.az: Google 不是作者；要写 TCL。

cards.en:
Think of it like this: A citation is a little sign-post in your essay pointing to where an idea came from; the reference list is the full address book at the end.

The rule:

  • In-text citation: cite the author and the year of publication in the body, e.g. Patrick (2008) found that…
  • Reference list: at the end of the article, full details.
  • APA pattern: Surname, Initial. (Year). Title. Place: Publisher.
  • CUHK (2020): the most extreme penalty for plagiarism, including self-plagiarism, is expulsion.

Exam wording: In-text citation cites the author and year of publication in the body; the reference list is attached at the end of the article.
cards.zh:
先这样理解：文内引用是文章里的“路牌”，指出意念来源；参考书目是文末的完整“通讯录”。

规则：

  • In-text citation：正文中写作者及出版年份，如 Patrick (2008) found that…
  • Reference list：文末列出完整资料。
  • APA：Surname, Initial. (Year). Title. Place: Publisher.
  • 中大 2020：抄袭（包括自我抄袭）最重可被开除。

考试写法（Exam wording）：In-text citation = author + year in the body; reference list = full details at the end.

ex.q: Author Mary Wong, book 'Smart City Data', 2019, XYZ Press, Hong Kong. Write both.
ex.a:
1. Reference: Wong, M. (2019). Smart City Data. Hong Kong: XYZ Press.
2. In-text: Wong (2019) found that…
ex.az: 按 APA 写两种。

ex.q: Book by David Lee, 'Coding Basics', 2021, ABC Press, Hong Kong. Reference entry?
ex.a:
1. Surname first: Lee, D.
2. (2021).
3. → Lee, D. (2021). Coding Basics. Hong Kong: ABC Press.
ex.az: 姓先、名缩写。

ex.q: Common mistake: "I reused my own old essay, so it can't be plagiarism."
ex.a:
1. Self-plagiarism counts too.
2. CUHK: may lead to expulsion.
3. Cite your earlier work like any other source.
ex.az: 自我抄袭也算抄袭。

cards.tz: 误解：抄袭 vs 侵犯版权
cards.en:
Think of it like this: Plagiarism is about honesty (did you say whose it is?). Infringement is about permission (were you allowed to copy?). You can fail one, the other, or both.

The rule:

PlagiarismCopyright infringement
NatureUnethicalIllegal
ProblemNo acknowledgementNo permission / beyond exceptions
FixCite the sourceGet permission / licence
  • Plagiarism means using another person's work without acknowledgement.
  • Images in slides for a class presentation: fair dealing (not infringement), but plagiarism without proper credit.

Exam wording: Copyright infringement may occur, but not always, in plagiarism, and vice versa. Plagiarism is unethical while copyright infringement is illegal.
cards.zh:
先这样理解：抄袭关乎“诚实”（有没有说是谁的？）；侵权关乎“许可”（有没有获准复制？）。可以犯其一或两者。

规则：

抄袭侵权
性质unethicalillegal
问题没注明出处没获许可
补救引用来源取得授权

考试写法（Exam wording）：Plagiarism is unethical while copyright infringement is illegal.

ex.q: Amy copies two paragraphs from a 19th-century public-domain novel into her essay without citation.
ex.a:
1. Public domain → no copyright → not infringement.
2. No acknowledgement → plagiarism.
ex.az: 抄袭但不侵权。

ex.q: Ben sells photocopies of a new textbook, crediting the author on the cover.
ex.a:
1. Credited → not plagiarism.
2. Copied and sold without permission → infringement.
ex.az: 侵权但不是抄袭。

ex.q: Common mistake: "Plagiarism always involves copyright infringement."
ex.a:
1. False: see Amy's case (public domain).
2. They are different: unethical vs illegal.
3. Check honesty and permission separately.
ex.az: 不一定。两者分开判断。

cards.tz: 版权持有人保护版权的方法
cards.en:
Think of it like this: If you made something, put a clear sign on it, register what needs registering, set the house rules, and decide who you let in.

The rule:

  1. State the copyright in your work (not legally necessary).
  2. Register corresponding IP such as patent.
  3. Set the terms of use of the granted copyright.
  4. Grant copyright for others to use your work.
  • Read agreements set by others: a social media site may obtain the right to reuse your uploaded content under its terms.
  • Notices: © All rights reserved; Some rights reserved (CC); Pixabay License (free commercial use, no attribution).

Exam wording: Copyright holders have a responsibility to set terms and conditions to limit the use of granted copyright, e.g. publishing with a CC licence.
cards.zh:
先这样理解：自己的作品：贴清楚标示、注册需要注册的、定好规矩、决定让谁使用。

规则：

  1. State 声明版权（法律上非必须）。
  2. Register 注册相关 IP（如专利）。
  3. Set 设定使用条款。
  4. Grant 授权他人使用。
  • 要读别人订的协议：社交平台可能取得重用你上传内容的权利。
  • 声明：© All rights reserved；Some rights reserved（CC）；Pixabay License。

考试写法（Exam wording）：Copyright holders have a responsibility to set terms and conditions to limit the use of granted copyright.

ex.q: Amy posts a vlog without a © notice. Can news media repost the whole vlog without permission?
ex.a:
1. Copyright is automatic; © not required.
2. Reposting the whole vlog is not limited fair dealing.
3. No, they need permission.
ex.az: 不可以，需获许可。

ex.q: A student photographer wants others to reuse her photos for non-profit projects with credit. What should she do?
ex.a:
1. Set terms: publish under CC BY-NC.
2. Add the CC notice.
ex.az: 用 CC BY-NC 发布。

ex.q: Common mistake: "Social media can never use my uploaded photos."
ex.a:
1. Its terms of use may grant it the right to reuse your content.
2. You agreed when signing up.
3. Read the agreement first.
ex.az: 平台条款可能容许重用，要先读协议。

cards.en:
Think of it like this: Buying software is like buying a cinema ticket: you get the right to watch, not the film itself.

The rule:

  • Copyright protects elements of software such as source code and interface design.
  • Licences are granted to users by developers to define how the software can be used or the restriction of certain usages.
  • Breaking the terms → may be copyright infringement.
  • 4 types: commercial, shareware, freeware, open source.
  • Buying software = buying a licence to use, not the copyright.

Exam wording: Licences are granted to users by developers to define how the software can be used or the restriction of certain usages.
cards.zh:
先这样理解：买软件像买电影票：你得到观看的权利，不是电影本身。

规则：

  • 版权保护软件的源代码和界面设计。
  • Licences … define how the software can be used or the restriction of certain usages.
  • 违反条款可能侵权。
  • 四类：commercial, shareware, freeware, open source。
  • 买软件 = 买使用权，不是版权。

考试写法（Exam wording）：Licences define how the software can be used or the restriction of certain usages.

ex.q: Patrick installed video editing software free for educational use. Now he has a paid freelance job. What should he do?
ex.a:
1. Read the licence agreement.
2. Check if commercial use is allowed.
3. If not, buy a commercial licence.
ex.az: 先读协议，看能否商用。

ex.q: A student gets Photoshop through a school education licence and wants to design paid posters for a shop.
ex.a:
1. Education licences are often non-commercial.
2. Paid work breaks the terms → may infringe.
3. Check the licence; buy a commercial one if needed.
ex.az: 教育授权多不可商用。

ex.q: Common mistake: "I paid for the app, so I own its copyright and can share it."
ex.a:
1. You bought a licence to use.
2. The developer keeps copyright.
3. Sharing copies breaks the licence.
ex.az: 付费 = 使用权，不能分享副本。

cards.t: Four types of software licence compared
cards.en:
Think of it like this: Four kinds of shops: a normal shop (pay), a free sample stall (try then pay), a free giveaway (take it, can't change it), and an open kitchen (free, and you can see and change the recipe).

The rule:

CommercialSharewareFreewareOpen source
PriceLicence feeFree trial (time/feature-limited); adsFreeFree
UsersSingle/multi/siteLike commercialUnlimitedUnlimited
Source codeNoNoNoYes: use, modify, copy, distribute
Copy / redistributeNoNoYesYes
Commercial useIn feeIn feeMaybe restrictedFree
SupportYesYesLimitedLimited
ExamplesMS Office, PhotoshopWinZip, Lightworks, PhotopeaChrome, Edge, WhatsApp, SignalLinux, Firefox, GIMP, Android

Tip from the book: shareware is very common on mobile platforms (free app, pay to unlock full features or remove ads).

Exam wording: Only open source software gives access to the source code. Shareware is a free trial that is time-limited or feature-limited.
cards.zh:
先这样理解：四种店：普通店（付钱）、试食摊（先试后买）、免费派发（拿走但不能改）、开放厨房（免费，可以看和改食谱）。

规则：

商业共享免费开源
价钱授权费免费试用（限时/限功能）免费免费
源代码无无无有
复制/分发否否可可
技术支持有有少少

课本提示：shareware 在手机平台非常常见（免费下载，付费解锁完整功能或去广告）。

考试写法（Exam wording）：Only open source software gives access to the source code.

ex.q: Software P is free and Lily may edit its code; Software Q is free for 30 days. Classify.
ex.a:
1. Q: time-limited trial → shareware.
2. P: free + code editable → open source.
ex.az: Q 共享软件；P 开源。

ex.q: Classify: Firefox, WinZip, Microsoft Office, WhatsApp.
ex.a: Firefox → open source; WinZip → shareware; MS Office → commercial; WhatsApp → freeware.
ex.az: 开源、共享、商业、免费。

ex.q: Common mistake: "Chrome is free, so it's open source."
ex.a:
1. Free ≠ open source.
2. Chrome is freeware: you cannot get and modify its source code.
3. Open source must give source code access.
ex.az: 免费不等于开源。

cards.t: Choosing a licence type as a user
cards.tz: 用户角度：选择软件类型
cards.en:
Think of it like this: Choosing software is like choosing a phone plan: pay more for service and support, or pay less and help yourself.

The rule:

ProsCons
CommercialFrequent updates, technical support, ads-freeHigher cost; cannot modify code
SharewareBasic features free; trial before buying; updates and supportCannot modify code; pay for full/premium; ads
FreewareFree; copy and redistribute freelyCannot modify code; less support; maybe personal use only
Open sourceFree; view/modify code; publish modified version; simpler licence purchaseLess technical support

Exam wording: For shareware: advanced features may be available only when you purchase and it is only free for the trial period.
cards.zh:
先这样理解：选软件像选电话计划：多付钱有服务支援，少付钱就要自己搞定。

规则：

优点缺点
商业常更新、技术支持、无广告贵、不能改代码
共享基本功能免费、可先试完整版要付费、有广告
免费免费、可分发不能改、支持少、或限个人用
开源免费、可看可改技术支持少

考试写法（Exam wording）：Shareware 缺点：advanced features only when you purchase；only free for the trial period。

ex.q: David wants video editing software for vlogs. One pro and con each for commercial and open source.
ex.a:
1. Commercial: pro = updates + support; con = higher cost.
2. Open source: pro = free, can modify; con = less support.
ex.az: 商业：支持好/贵；开源：免费可改/支持少。

ex.q: A small NGO with no IT staff and little money needs an office suite. Suggest a type with a reason.
ex.a:
1. Little money → avoid commercial.
2. Open source (e.g. OpenOffice): free, no licence purchasing.
3. Accept less support, or use community help.
ex.az: 开源：免费，但支持少。

ex.q: Common mistake: "A disadvantage of shareware is that others may modify its source code."
ex.a:
1. Shareware does not release source code.
2. Real cons: pay for advanced features, free only for the trial.
ex.az: 共享软件不公开源代码，此说错。

cards.t: Choosing a licence type as a developer
cards.tz: 开发者角度：选择授权模式
cards.en:
Think of it like this: As a maker you choose: sell tickets (money, fewer users), give free samples with ads, give it away (fame), or open the kitchen to helpers (teamwork).

The rule:

ProsCons
CommercialEarn from each purchase/subscription; users can't copy/redistributeFewer users
SharewareEarn from ads; persuade users to buy during trialNo income if ads blocked or users don't pay
FreewareUsers can't modify code; can redistribute; more usersNo licence income
Open sourceUsers study/modify code; co-develop with users; more usersNo licence income

Exam wording: Shareware lets a developer make money for authorising use, not give up copyright, and attract more people to try it.
cards.zh:
先这样理解：作为开发者你可以：卖票（有钱、用户少）、广告+试用、免费派（多人用）、开放厨房（大家一起改）。

规则：

优点缺点
商业每次购买有收入用户少
共享广告收入、试用期说服购买用户屏蔽广告/不付费就没收入
免费不让人改代码、多人用无授权收入
开源与用户合作开发、多人用无授权收入

考试写法（Exam wording）：Shareware：make money for authorising use, not give up copyright, attract more people to try it。

ex.q: An indie developer wants many users, no code changes by others, and doesn't need income. Which licence?
ex.a:
1. Many users + redistribution → free.
2. No modification → source not released.
3. → Freeware.
ex.az: 免费软件。

ex.q: A university team wants volunteers worldwide to help fix bugs. Which licence?
ex.a:
1. Others must read and modify code.
2. → Open source: cooperate with users to develop.
ex.az: 开源。

ex.q: Common mistake: "Publish as shareware so others can improve the source code together."
ex.a:
1. Improving code together is a reason for open source.
2. Shareware hides the source code.
3. Shareware reasons: income, keep copyright, attract trials.
ex.az: 一起改代码是开源的理由。

cards.t: Misconception: freeware and open source are not uncopyrighted
cards.tz: 误解：免费及开源软件也有版权
cards.en:
Think of it like this: A free gift still has a giver. Free and open source software still belong to their authors; they just let you use them under rules.

The rule:

  • Only public domain software is uncopyrighted.
  • Freeware, shareware, open source and commercial software only grant users rights to use the software under different licence agreements.
  • Breaking open source terms (e.g. removing the licence notice) can still be infringement.
  • If Lily modifies open source Software P, the original author keeps copyright of the original code; Lily owns only her new contributions.
  • Similarity: freeware and open source are both free to use, copy and redistribute. Difference: only open source allows access to and modification of the source code.

Exam wording: Only public domain software is uncopyrighted. Freeware, shareware, open source and commercial software only grant users rights to use the software under different licence agreements.
cards.zh:
先这样理解：免费礼物也有送礼人。免费和开源软件仍属作者，只是按规则让你用。

规则：

  • Only public domain software is uncopyrighted.
  • 四类软件都只是按不同协议授予使用权。
  • 违反开源条款（如删除授权声明）仍可侵权。
  • Lily 改了开源软件 P，原作者仍拥有原代码版权，Lily 只拥有自己新增部分。
  • 相同：都可免费使用、复制、分发。不同：只有开源可取得及修改源代码。

考试写法（Exam wording）：Only public domain software is uncopyrighted.

ex.q: One similarity and one difference between freeware and open source.
ex.a:
1. Similarity: both free to use, copy, redistribute.
2. Difference: only open source gives access to modify source code.
ex.az: 同：免费可分发；异：只有开源可改源码。

ex.q: Lily modifies most of Software P (open source) and redistributes it. Who owns what?
ex.a:
1. Original author keeps copyright of original code.
2. Lily owns her new contributions.
3. She must follow the open source licence.
ex.az: 原作者保留原代码版权；Lily 拥有新部分。

ex.q: Common mistake: "Freeware is free, so I can sell it on my website."
ex.a:
1. Freeware is still copyrighted.
2. Licence allows free use/redistribution, not selling or modifying.
3. Selling it = infringement.
ex.az: 免费软件仍有版权，不能拿来卖。

cards.t: User licence: single-user, multi-user and site licence
cards.tz: 用户授权：单用户、多用户、场地授权
cards.en:
Think of it like this: A single-user licence is a one-person ticket. A multi-user licence is a group ticket. A site licence is a pass for everyone inside one building.

The rule:

  • Commercial/shareware licences state the number of authorised users for each licence.
  • Single-user licence: installed on only one device or only one user can use the software at a time.
  • Multi-user / site licence: unlimited or a defined number of users from a company, organisation or institute.
  • A site licence may limit use to a particular location.
  • Family subscription plan (book TIP): a defined number of users who live together can use the premium functions at a time.

Exam wording: A single-user licence allows the software to be installed on only one device or used by only one user at a time.
cards.zh:
先这样理解：单用户授权是一人票；多用户授权是团体票；场地授权是一栋楼里人人可用的通行证。

规则：

  • 授权会注明授权用户数目。
  • Single-user licence：只可装在一部装置或同一时间一人使用。
  • Multi-user / site licence：公司/机构内无限或指定数目用户。
  • Site licence 可能限制在特定地点使用。
  • 家庭订阅计划（课本 TIP）：同住的指定数目用户可同时使用付费功能。

考试写法（Exam wording）：single-user: only one device / one user at a time；site licence: may limit use at a particular location。

ex.q: A school with 40 PCs buys one single-user licence and activates it on all PCs. Problem and fix?
ex.a:
1. Allows only 1 device → 39 unauthorised copies.
2. = copyright infringement.
3. Fix: buy a site licence or a multi-user licence for 40.
ex.az: 39 份未授权；改买场地/多用户授权。

ex.q: A company has 10 staff who all need the software at the same time. How many single-user licences?
ex.a:
1. Single-user = one user at a time.
2. 10 people at once → 10 licences (or one 10-user multi-user licence).
ex.az: 10 份或一个 10 人授权。

ex.q: Common mistake: "With a site licence, staff can install it at home too."
ex.a:
1. A site licence may limit use to a particular location.
2. Home is outside the site.
3. Read the agreement before installing elsewhere.
ex.az: 场地授权可能只限该地点。

cards.en:
Think of it like this: Instead of buying a car, you pay monthly for a ride app. SaaS is renting software that lives on the company's computers in the cloud.

The rule:

  • Old: one-off licence fee. New: subscription model that treats software as a service, paid monthly or annually.
  • SaaS is also known as web-based software because it is centrally hosted by the software company based on cloud computing.
  • Provider hosts servers, database, code, application, help desk; business, institutional and personal users connect over the Internet.
  • Examples: Microsoft 365, Adobe Creative Cloud, Zoom, Teams, Spotify, Netflix.

Exam wording: SaaS is also known as web-based software because it is centrally hosted by the software company based on cloud computing; users pay for the licence monthly or annually.
cards.zh:
先这样理解：不买车，按月付钱用叫车 app。SaaS 就是“租用”放在公司云端电脑上的软件。

规则：

  • 旧：one-off licence fee；新：subscription，每月或每年付费。
  • SaaS is also known as web-based software because it is centrally hosted … based on cloud computing.
  • 供应商在云端管理服务器、数据库、代码、应用、支援；用户经互联网使用。
  • 例：Microsoft 365、Adobe CC、Zoom、Spotify、Netflix。

考试写法（Exam wording）：SaaS … centrally hosted by the software company based on cloud computing。

ex.q: Why is SaaS also called web-based software?
ex.a:
1. Software is centrally hosted by the company on cloud servers.
2. Users access it through the Internet.
3. Not installed and run fully locally.
ex.az: 集中托管于云端，经互联网使用。

ex.q: A school moves from installed Office 2016 to Microsoft 365. Name two changes for IT staff.
ex.a:
1. No need to manage installation/servers; updates applied centrally.
2. Must pay yearly and need Internet.
ex.az: 不用管安装更新；要年费和网络。

ex.q: Common mistake: "After I cancel my Spotify subscription, I still own the songs I saved."
ex.a:
1. SaaS = paying for access, not ownership.
2. When the subscription ends, access stops.
ex.az: 订阅结束即失去使用权。

frames.en: The company hosts servers, database, code and help desk in the cloud.
frames.zh: 供应商在云端托管一切。

frames.en: User pays monthly/annually and logs in with an account.
frames.zh: 用户按月/年付费并登入。

frames.en: Requests and data travel over the Internet; the app runs on the provider's servers.
frames.zh: 经互联网使用，程序在供应商服务器运行。

frames.en: Updates are installed centrally, so every user gets them at once.
frames.zh: 集中更新，全部用户同时获得。

cards.tz: 永久授权 vs 订阅
cards.en:
Think of it like this: Buying a book (pay once, keep forever, works offline) vs a library membership (pay monthly, always the newest books, but you need to go there).

The rule:

Perpetual licenceSubscription
ProsIndefinite use with one-off payment; no Internet needed; faster response; better security control (no data on cloud)Trial period; cloud backup; simpler installation; multiple devices by login; free frequent updates and support
ConsExtra costs for maintenance/updates; limited to a certain number of devicesInternet may be required; longer response time
ExamplesOffice Home and Student 2019; Adobe CS6Netflix, Spotify, Zoom, Adobe CC, Microsoft 365

Exam wording: Perpetual: indefinite use with one-off payment, Internet connection not required. Subscription: access on multiple devices by account login, free frequent updates.
cards.zh:
先这样理解：买书（付一次、永远拥有、离线可读）vs 图书馆会员（按月付、总有新书，但要去馆）。

规则：

永久授权订阅
优点一次付款永久使用；不需上网；反应快；保安较好有试用期；云端备份；安装简单；多装置登入；免费更新与支援
缺点维护/更新另收费；限装置数目或需上网；反应较慢

考试写法（Exam wording）：永久：one-off payment, Internet not required；订阅：multiple devices by login, free frequent updates。

ex.q: A law firm with confidential files and unreliable Internet: perpetual or subscription? Two reasons.
ex.a:
1. Perpetual.
2. Works without Internet.
3. Better security control: no data sent to cloud.
ex.az: 永久授权：不需网络、保安较好。

ex.q: A freelancer works on a desktop, laptop and tablet and wants the newest features. Which?
ex.a:
1. Subscription.
2. Multiple devices by account login.
3. Free frequent updates + cloud backup.
ex.az: 订阅。

ex.q: Common mistake: "A perpetual licence means I get all future versions free forever."
ex.a:
1. Perpetual = use this version forever.
2. Additional costs may be charged for updates/maintenance.
ex.az: 永久授权不包括所有新版本。

cards.en:
Think of it like this: Anyone can copy a lock-box, but it won't open without the key. The installer is the box; the licence key is the key only paying customers get.

The rule:

  • Licence key (activation key, product key): a string of characters given to an authorised user who has paid for the software.
  • During installation, the user enters the licence key to register or activate the software.
  • Copied installer alone is useless; vendor can limit activations per key.
  • Hardware key (USB dongle): a physical device plugged into USB for unlocking the software; also used for two-factor authentication.
  • Licence keys support device-locked and user-locked licences.

Exam wording: A licence key is a string of characters given to an authorised user who has paid for the software; it is entered during installation to register or activate the software.
cards.zh:
先这样理解：谁都能复制一个锁箱，但没钥匙打不开。安装档是箱，序号就是只有付费用户才有的钥匙。

规则：

  • Licence key：a string of characters given to an authorised user who has paid。
  • 安装时输入序号以注册或启动软件。
  • 只复制安装档没用；厂商可限制每个序号的启动次数。
  • Hardware key（USB dongle）：插入 USB 以解锁软件，也可作双重认证。

考试写法（Exam wording）：a string of characters given to an authorised user who has paid … entered to register or activate the software。

ex.q: Why does a licence key reduce piracy compared with only selling a downloadable installer?
ex.a:
1. Installer can be copied freely.
2. Software won't run without a valid key given only to payers.
3. Vendor limits activations, so sharing one key fails.
ex.az: 无序号不能运行，且限启动次数。

ex.q: A CAD program only runs when a USB dongle is plugged in. What is this and why use it?
ex.a:
1. Hardware key.
2. Physical, so hard to copy like a text key.
3. Unlocks the software only for the holder.
ex.az: 硬件钥匙，难复制。

ex.q: Common mistake: "I'll post my key online so my friends can activate too; it's my key."
ex.a:
1. The key is given to one authorised paying user.
2. Sharing it = unauthorised use; activations will also be blocked.
ex.az: 序号只授权给付费用户，分享即违规。

frames.en: User pays and receives a licence key (e.g. ABCDE-12345-…).
User installs the software; it asks for the key.
Software sends the key to the vendor; vendor checks it is valid and counts activations.
frames.zh: 软件把序号送往厂商检查。

frames.en: Valid → activated. Too many activations or fake key → 'Invalid licence key'.
frames.zh: 有效则启动，否则显示 Invalid licence key。

cards.tz: 锁定装置 vs 锁定用户授权
cards.en:
Think of it like this: Device-locked = the key is glued to one computer. User-locked = the key follows you (your account) to any computer you sign in on.

The rule:

Device-lockedUser-locked
Locked toMachine ID (unique code of a device)User account
DevicesSingle device (some allow a few)Any device while signed in
UsersOne at a timeUsually one at a time
ActivationKey + machine ID at installationRegistration; agree to terms
  • Too many activations → 'Invalid licence key'.
  • User-locked is an example of a floating licence (install on multiple devices).

Exam wording: Device-locked: the licence key is locked to the unique machine ID of your device. User-locked: the licence key is locked to a specific account; users can use it on any device but must remain signed in.
cards.zh:
先这样理解：锁定装置 = 序号黏在一部电脑上；锁定用户 = 序号跟着你的帐户走，任何电脑登入即可。

规则：

锁定装置锁定用户
锁定于Machine ID用户帐户
装置单一（或少数）任何（须登入）
启动安装时绑定机器码注册、同意条款
  • 超出次数 → 'Invalid licence key'。
  • User-locked 是 floating licence 的一种。

考试写法（Exam wording）：locked to the unique machine ID vs locked to a specific account … remain signed in。

ex.q: Kelly reinstalls a device-locked program on her new laptop with the same key and gets 'Invalid licence key'. Why?
ex.a:
1. Key was locked to the old machine ID.
2. Maximum activations reached.
3. Deactivate old device or contact vendor.
ex.az: 序号绑定旧机器码且已达上限。

ex.q: Adobe CC lets Joe use the app on home and school PCs after signing in. Which type?
ex.a:
1. Locked to his account, any device, must stay signed in.
2. → User-locked (floating licence).
ex.az: 锁定用户。

ex.q: Common mistake: "User-locked means my whole family can use it at the same time on different devices."
ex.a:
1. It is locked to one account.
2. Single-user licence: usually one user at a time.
3. Family needs a family/multi-user plan.
ex.az: 通常同一时间一人；家人要买家庭计划。

cards.en:
Think of it like this: A visible watermark is a big stamp across a photo. An invisible one is like secret ink: you can't see it, but a special tool can read it, even after the photo is cut or shrunk.

The rule:

  • Digital watermark technology is embedding data into a digital work (images, videos, text…).
  • Visible: a mark made clear to the user.
  • Invisible: embedded but cannot be seen, and extracted using watermarking algorithms.
  • Invisible is popular: harder to remove, does not affect the carrying object, remains and can be extracted after cropping, resizing and compression.
  • Insertion: original + watermark bits → watermarked data. Extraction: modified copy → watermark still found.

Exam wording: Invisible watermarks are harder to remove, do not affect the carrying object, and can still be extracted even after cropping, resizing and compression.
cards.zh:
先这样理解：可见水印是盖在相片上的大印章；隐形水印像隐形墨水：看不到，但特别工具可读出，即使相片被裁剪或缩小。

规则：

  • Digital watermark: embedding data into a digital work。
  • Visible：用户看得见。
  • Invisible：看不见，用 watermarking algorithms 提取。
  • 隐形水印较受欢迎：难移除、不影响作品、裁剪/缩放/压缩后仍可提取。

考试写法（Exam wording）：Invisible watermarks are harder to remove, do not affect the carrying object, and can be extracted after cropping, resizing and compression.

ex.q: A photographer sells photos online. Two reasons to use an invisible rather than a visible watermark.
ex.a:
1. Does not affect the photo for paying customers.
2. Harder to remove, survives cropping/compression, so ownership can be proved.
ex.az: 不影响相片；难移除。

ex.q: A pirate crops and compresses a watermarked image. Can the owner still prove ownership?
ex.a:
1. Run the watermarking algorithm on the pirated copy.
2. Invisible watermark remains unchanged.
3. Yes, it is extracted as proof.
ex.az: 仍可提取水印证明。

ex.q: Common mistake: "I removed the visible watermark, so the photo is now free to use."
ex.a:
1. Removing a watermark doesn't remove copyright.
2. Uploading it is still infringement.
ex.az: 移除水印不等于没有版权。

frames.en: Original image + watermark bits (0101 1100 0110) → algorithm hides bits in the pixels.
frames.zh: 原图 + 水印位元 → 算法嵌入。

frames.en: The watermarked image looks the same to the eye.
Pirate crops, resizes and compresses the image.
Algorithm extracts 0101 1100 0110 from the modified copy → proves ownership.
frames.zh: 算法从修改后副本提取水印 → 证明拥有权。

cards.en:
Think of it like this: Give each friend a copy of a secret with a different hidden mark. If it leaks, the mark tells you whose copy it was.

The rule:

ApplicationMethod
Digital copyright protectionOwnership rights are embedded to prove copyright infringement.
Source tracingData given to different recipients is watermarked differently, to trace the person who leaks confidential information.
  • Alibaba (2016) traced the employee who leaked a screenshot of internal news using digital watermarks.
  • To stop unauthorised distribution of images → digital watermark (not digital signature, not SSL).

Exam wording: Data given to different recipients is watermarked differently. This is useful to trace the person who leaks the confidential information.
cards.zh:
先这样理解：给每个朋友一份秘密，各藏不同记号。泄露时，记号就告诉你是谁那份。

规则：

应用方法
Digital copyright protection嵌入拥有权以证明侵权
Source tracing给不同收件人不同水印，追查泄密者
  • 阿里巴巴 2016 年以水印追查泄露截图的员工。
  • 防止图片被未授权分发 → 数码水印（不是数码签署、SSL）。

考试写法（Exam wording）：Data given to different recipients is watermarked differently … to trace the person who leaks the confidential information.

ex.q: A company sends a confidential PDF to 5 partners and a copy leaks. How to find the leaker?
ex.a:
1. Before sending, embed a different invisible watermark (partner ID) in each copy.
2. Extract it from the leaked copy.
3. The ID shows whose copy leaked.
ex.az: 每份嵌入不同 ID，提取即知。

ex.q: A streaming site wants to stop its videos being re-uploaded elsewhere. Which technology helps?
ex.a:
1. Embed ownership with digital watermarks.
2. Pirated uploads can be detected and proven.
ex.az: 数码水印。

ex.q: Common mistake: "Use a digital signature to prevent unauthorised distribution of images."
ex.a:
1. Digital signature verifies the sender and detects modification.
2. SSL encrypts data in transit.
3. Stopping image redistribution → digital watermark.
ex.az: 应选数码水印。

cards.en:
Think of it like this: Like a wax seal on a royal letter: you know who sent it, and if anyone opened and changed it, the seal is broken.

The rule:

  • Digital signature is a technology used for verifying the sender's identity.
  • Commonly applied in detecting unauthorised modification and forgery (贗品) such as pirated software.
  • The company signs its program files. If a pirate cracks or adds malware, the signature no longer matches.
  • Check on Windows: right-click → Properties → Digital Signatures tab → signer name, digest algorithm, timestamp.
  • Watermark = ownership/trace source; signature = who sent it and not modified.

Exam wording: Digital signature is used for verifying the sender's identity and detecting unauthorised modification and forgery such as pirated software.
cards.zh:
先这样理解：像皇室信件上的火漆印：知道是谁寄的；若有人拆开改动，印就破了。

规则：

  • Digital signature … verifying the sender's identity.
  • 用于侦测未经授权的修改和伪造（如盗版软件）。
  • 公司为程序签署；盗版者破解或加入恶意程序后，签署不再吻合。
  • Windows：右键 → Properties → Digital Signatures → 签署人、摘要算法、时间。

考试写法（Exam wording）：verifying the sender's identity … detecting unauthorised modification and forgery such as pirated software。

ex.q: You download an installer claiming to be from Adobe. How do you check it is genuine?
ex.a:
1. Right-click → Properties → Digital Signatures.
2. Signer should be the real company (e.g. Adobe Systems) and valid.
3. Missing/invalid → modified or forged.
ex.az: 查看数码签署。

ex.q: A cracked game was edited to skip licence checks. Why does Windows warn the signature is invalid?
ex.a:
1. Original files were signed by the developer.
2. Any change makes the file no longer match the signature.
3. So modification is detected.
ex.az: 修改后签署不吻合。

ex.q: Common mistake: "A digital signature stops people from copying the program."
ex.a:
1. It does not stop copying.
2. It verifies sender and detects modification.
3. To prove ownership/trace copies → watermark; to stop use → licence key.
ex.az: 签署不能阻止复制，只验证来源和完整性。

demo.title: How a digital signature detects tampering

frames.en: Developer signs the program file with its private key.
frames.zh: 开发商用私钥签署程序。

frames.en: User downloads the file with its signature.
User's computer checks the signature with the developer's public key.
Match → genuine, unmodified. Mismatch → modified or forged (e.g. pirated).
frames.zh: 吻合 → 正版；不吻合 → 被改/伪造。

cards.tz: 必须上网的应用：以加密防盗版
cards.en:
Think of it like this: The game keeps its most important parts (your coins, HP) locked in the company's safe. Each time you play, the safe sends you a locked box only the real app can open.

The rule:

  1. User opens the game; it connects to the Internet.
  2. The server performs data encryption on important data/commands, e.g. in-game currency, HP, MP.
  3. Server sends encrypted data to the device.
  4. The device performs data decryption and runs the game.
  • Aim: prevent illegal modification of the app such as cheating and pirated games.
  • Cost: no offline mode; uses mobile data.

Exam wording: When the game connects to the Internet, it is processing data encryption and decryption, which aims to prevent illegal modification of the app such as cheating and pirated games.
cards.zh:
先这样理解：游戏把最重要的部分（金币、HP）锁在公司的保险箱。每次玩，保险箱寄来一个只有正版 app 打得开的锁盒。

规则：

  1. 用户开游戏，连上网。
  2. 服务器把重要数据（游戏币、HP、MP）加密。
  3. 传送加密数据到装置。
  4. 装置解密后运行游戏。
  • 目的：prevent illegal modification of the app such as cheating and pirated games。
  • 代价：不能离线、耗流量。

考试写法（Exam wording）：… processing data encryption and decryption … to prevent illegal modification of the app such as cheating and pirated games.

ex.q: A single-player game shows 'No Connection – Try Again' offline. How does this protect the developer's IP?
ex.a:
1. Key data are encrypted on the server.
2. Only decrypted on the device after connecting.
3. Pirated/modified copies can't get valid data → stops piracy and cheating.
ex.az: 服务器加密关键数据，盗版无法取得。

ex.q: A player edits the local save file to give himself 999,999 coins. Why doesn't it work in an online-only game?
ex.a:
1. Coin values come from the server, encrypted.
2. The local edit is ignored/overwritten.
3. Cheating by modifying the app fails.
ex.az: 币值来自服务器，改本地无效。

ex.q: Common mistake: "It needs Internet only because of online multiplayer."
ex.a:
1. Even single-player games may need it.
2. The connection is for encryption/decryption of key data.
3. Purpose: anti-piracy and anti-cheating.
ex.az: 联网是为加密解密以防盗版作弊。

frames.en: The game app connects to the developer's server.
Server encrypts coins, HP, MP and commands.
Encrypted data travel to the device.
The genuine app decrypts and runs. A cracked offline copy gets nothing.
frames.zh: 正版 app 解密运行；破解版无法取得。

mc.q: Which of the following actions may be seen as copyright infringement?
o: Broadcasting a school event with permission.
Downloading articles from an academic database.
Sending selfies to friends using peer-to-peer (P2P) software.
Uploading films to the cloud storage and sharing them with friends.
mc.e: Sharing copyrighted films without permission is unauthorised distribution (Internet piracy).
mc.ez: 未经许可分享电影属互联网盗版。
mc.src: Textbook E Ch3 Chapter Exercise MC1 (p.108)

mc.q: Janice takes the following actions on her work computer. Which of them is considered legal?
o: Buying a CD and using the music in an event promotional video.
Using peer-to-peer (P2P) software to download a movie for personal use.
Sending freeware to colleagues via a BT program.
Sharing a commercial software with friends via the cloud.
mc.e: Freeware may be copied and redistributed freely.
mc.ez: 免费软件可自由复制及分发。
mc.src: Textbook E Ch3 Chapter Exercise MC2 (p.108)

mc.q: Which may be considered copyright infringement? (1) Screenshot of a free online newspaper posted on social media (2) Using photos from an official website to sell a used product online (3) Photocopying one page of a 36-page recipe book for a school assignment (4) Removing the watermark from a copyrighted photo and uploading it to a personal website
mc.e: (3) is limited use for education (fair dealing); the others use works without permission.
mc.src: Textbook E Ch3 Chapter Exercise MC3 (p.108)

mc.q: Which of the following statements correctly describes copyright in Hong Kong?
o: Copyright owners cannot transfer their copyrights to others.
Copyright only protects high quality works.
Copyright owners are required to put a copyright symbol '©' on their work for a higher level of copyright protection.
mc.e: Copyright is given automatically when a work is completed; no registration or notice is needed.
mc.ez: 版权自动产生，毋须注册或声明。
mc.src: Textbook E Ch3 Chapter Exercise MC4 (p.108)

mc.q: Which of the following statements about freeware is correct?
o: Distribution of the software is not allowed.
The software is free to make copies.
The software is allowed to be installed on a single device only.
The source code is free to modify.
mc.e: Freeware: unlimited users, copying and redistribution allowed, no source code access.
mc.ez: 免费软件可复制，但不能改源码。
mc.src: Textbook E Ch3 Chapter Exercise MC5 (p.108)
